claim: Compiler-generated process initialization and per-Worker setup under a preflighted shared owner layout; lazy installation in two late Workers preserves all foreign regions, mutated shared cells, runtime sentinels and original published code.
owner: Trusted synchronous initialization owner. Atomic process state 0/1/2/3 means fresh/initializing/ready/failed. A layout digest is published before ready and checked by late Workers. Each Worker claims its own state once; no spinning or implicit retry. A callback failure poisons its Worker and, during bootstrap, the process; it is not rollback.
generated: Five freshly compiled unchanged-backend B modules: process initializer, Worker initializer, reader, mutator and indirect reader caller. Native CCL compiles and executes the same forms. Worker setup calls its reader through a lazy table entry. The original Worker stays alive and executes published code again after both late Workers.
layout: Canonical objects, generated functions and imported symbols, code registry, shared runtime BSS/staging sentinels, atomic admission control, and three disjoint Worker TCR/value/temp/control stacks, allocation regions, binding vectors, cells and staging regions. TCR v2 offsets bound explicitly; module/object counts derive extents. No C service is linked, so no C stack or static/BSS region is present. Stack minima are declared owner resource budgets; generated guards enforce actual call demand.
limits: Shared Node/V8 qualification only; no browser, JSPI, unshared runtime, concurrent Lisp execution, concurrent collection or process restart claim.

Fresh shared memory belongs to one trusted owner. Layout digests are identity checks against trusted metadata, not signing or adversarial code confinement. Generated initializers are trusted code; their actual writes are tested with foreign-region digests and boundary canaries.
Initialization is synchronous. A failed callback may have written its owned regions; state is terminal rather than rolled back. Busy and failed process states refuse instead of waiting.

Worker creation is deliberately ordered after mutation and publication. Tables are Worker-local Wasm tables; code identities and registry bytes are process-shared. Slot zero remains reserved, and lazy installation publishes only declared slots.
This is a bounded bootstrap ownership profile, not a production thread scheduler, production package membership, image cross-dump or the Stage 2 Worker-creation qualification.

The corpus has no literal pool bytes and uses no C services; omitted zero-length storage is explicit. Runtime constructors, GC and numerical services retain their own ownership and admission obligations.
